title: AI Search Engines for Source Discovery and Answers
description: Compare AI search engines for finding sources and synthesizing answers. Review citation quality, freshness, search scope, and how uncertainty is communicated.
introduction: AI search engines combine information discovery with generated answers or summaries. They can help orient a question, find useful sources, and compare material without opening every result first. The important boundary is between what a source actually supports and what the system synthesizes or infers. This category focuses on finding information beyond a supplied document; document chat works with an uploaded collection, and general assistants may offer search as only one feature.
capabilities: Find relevant pages or documents in the search scope the service supports.
Synthesize a response from retrieved material with available source references.
Refine a question through follow-up searches and conversational exploration.
Organize discovered sources for comparison, reading, or a subsequent research task.

audiences.label: Research readers
audiences.text: Build an initial source map for an unfamiliar question, then open important references and check the evidence before writing conclusions.

audiences.label: Business teams
audiences.text: Investigate a current market or product question, separating dated source facts from generated interpretations that need additional confirmation.

criteria.label: Citation usefulness
criteria.text: Check whether references support the associated claims and lead to accessible source passages rather than merely related pages.

criteria.label: Coverage and freshness
criteria.text: Assess search scope, date controls, regional coverage, and access limitations for the kinds of information your questions require.

criteria.label: Uncertainty and comparison
criteria.text: Look for clear treatment of conflicting sources, missing evidence, and qualified conclusions rather than an overly definite single answer.

workflow: Frame a specific question with its time period, location, and any preferred source types.
Inspect the generated answer and open the key references, checking dates, context, and support for individual claims.
Refine gaps or disagreements with further searches and keep a source list for the final research output.

faqs.question: Are citations enough to trust an AI search answer?
faqs.answer: No. Open the cited material and check whether it supports the exact statement, including dates and qualifications. A relevant-looking link can still fail to establish the claim placed beside it.

faqs.question: How is AI search different from document chat?
faqs.answer: AI search discovers information across its available search sources. Document chat primarily answers from material you provide or connect. Choose based on whether you need discovery or analysis of a known collection.

faqs.question: Can I rely on an answer about a recent event?
faqs.answer: Check source publication dates and the dates of the underlying events. Look for current primary evidence and conflicting updates rather than assuming a generated answer reflects the latest available information.

faqs.question: What should I do when sources disagree?
faqs.answer: Identify whether they discuss the same period, definitions, and circumstances. Read the primary evidence where available, preserve unresolved differences, and avoid combining incompatible claims into a falsely certain conclusion.

faqs.question: When should I use a specialist research database?
faqs.answer: Use one when your task requires coverage, filters, or source types a general search service cannot establish. AI search can help orient the question, but it should not imply exhaustive discovery.
